headline_marked: India court rules [[Telegram ban was legal]] to stop medical exam leaks
headline: India court rules Telegram ban was legal to stop medical exam leaks
summary: A New Delhi court rejected Telegram's bid to overturn a temporary block, ruling that the government's actions to preserve exam integrity were reasonable.
details: A New Delhi court has ruled that the Indian government's temporary ban on Telegram from June 16 to June 22 was legal and reasonable. The block was aimed at preserving the integrity of a key medical school entrance exam.
The government implemented the ban after results for the medical school exams were scrapped last month following allegations that the question paper had been leaked.
Justice Tejas Karia stated that the government is empowered to issue directions for blocking public access to the app to prevent such leaks.
Telegram, which has over 150 million users in India, had challenged the order. The company claimed it proactively removed over 900 links containing unlawful exam-related content.
Digital rights groups, including the Internet Freedom Foundation, warned that the verdict sets a concerning precedent for the open internet and free speech rights.
The Indian government argued that Telegram's features, such as easy recreation of blocked channels and concealed usernames, created a persistent enforcement challenge.
Founder Pavel Durov criticized the ban, stating it punished users while the leaks simply moved to other platforms.
caption:
A New Delhi court has upheld the Indian government's temporary ban on Telegram, ruling it was necessary to stop medical exam leaks.

A New Delhi court has ruled that the Indian government's temporary ban on Telegram from June 16 to June 22 was legal and reasonable. The block was aimed at preserving the integrity of a key medical school entrance exam.

The government implemented the ban after results for the medical school exams were scrapped last month following allegations that the question paper had been leaked.

Justice Tejas Karia stated that the government is empowered to issue directions for blocking public access to the app to prevent such leaks.

Telegram, which has over 150 million users in India, had challenged the order. The company claimed it proactively removed over 900 links containing unlawful exam-related content.

Digital rights groups, including the Internet Freedom Foundation, warned that the verdict sets a concerning precedent for the open internet and free speech rights.

The Indian government argued that Telegram's features, such as easy recreation of blocked channels and concealed usernames, created a persistent enforcement challenge.

Founder Pavel Durov criticized the ban, stating it punished users while the leaks simply moved to other platforms.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star

headline_marked: 11-year-old [[domestic worker dies after fall]] from Dhanmondi building
headline: 11-year-old domestic worker dies after fall from Dhanmondi building
summary: The child, Rikta Akter, reportedly fell from the 10th floor. Her father alleges murder and demands a full investigation into the death.
details: An 11-year-old house help, Rikta Akter, died after reportedly falling from the 10th floor of a 12-storey building in Dhaka's Dhanmondi area early today.
The incident occurred around 6:30am on Road 9/A. Rikta was rushed to Ibn Sina Hospital, where doctors pronounced her dead.
Building staff reported hearing a loud sound and finding the girl lying on the ground behind the building, bleeding and breathing heavily before she passed away.
The child had been working at an apartment on the 10th floor since the beginning of this month. The apartment was occupied by a family of four.
Rikta's father, Md Shahin Mia, stated that the girl was sent to work through an agent in exchange for Tk 10,000 about a month ago.
The father alleged that during a video call a week ago, he noticed swelling on his daughter's face, which led him to ask the agent to bring her home.
Md Shahin Mia has alleged that his daughter was murdered and is demanding justice and severe punishment for those responsible.
Police are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the death to determine if it was an accident or foul play.

The child had been working at an apartment on the 10th floor since the beginning of this month. The apartment was occupied by a family of four.

Rikta's father, Md Shahin Mia, stated that the girl was sent to work through an agent in exchange for Tk 10,000 about a month ago.

The father alleged that during a video call a week ago, he noticed swelling on his daughter's face, which led him to ask the agent to bring her home.
